questions.q: You are driving a scheduled bus and approaching a stop to let passengers off. May you stop at the zigzag markings?
options: No: no one may stop at marking 1.17 or within 15 m of it
Yes, but only if there are no other buses at the stop
Yes, but only with the dispatcher's permission
Yes: the ban does not apply to category M2 and M3 buses
questions.explain: Marking 1.17 marks a route vehicle stop. The ban on stopping in the stop area and within 15 m of it does not apply to buses of categories M2 and M3.

questions.q: Your friend is waiting at a bus stop. May you stop at the zigzag markings for a minute so that your friend can get in?
options: Yes: picking up a passenger is stopping, not parking
Yes, if there is no bus at the stop at the moment
Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights and stay in the car
No: passenger cars are prohibited from stopping there
questions.explain: Marking 1.17 marks a route vehicle stop. Passenger cars must not stop in the stop area or within 15 m of it, even to pick up a passenger.

questions.q: Under sign 3.28, a van driver spends 15 minutes unloading goods for a shop. Is he breaking the rules?
options: Yes: he has been there over 5 minutes, so it is already parking
No, but only if his hazard warning lights are on
Yes: under this sign you may unload for no more than 5 minutes at a time
No: unloading is stopping, and the sign prohibits only parking
questions.explain: A halt for loading or unloading counts as stopping, even if it lasts longer than 5 minutes. Sign 3.28 prohibits only parking, so the van driver is not breaking any rules.

questions.q: In which of these cases is stopping prohibited?
options: Your van would hide traffic light signals from other drivers
You would stop 10 m after a pedestrian crossing
You would stop 20 m from a yard exit without blocking it
You would stop on a bridge with three lanes in your direction
questions.explain: Stopping is prohibited where a vehicle would hide traffic light signals or road signs from other drivers. The other places listed are allowed for stopping: there is no ban after a crossing, a yard exit is not an intersection, and you may stop on a bridge with three lanes in your direction.

questions.q: Where do the Rules prohibit both stopping and parking?
options: On the shoulder outside a built-up area
At the left-hand edge of a one-way street in a built-up area
20 m after a bus stop
On lawns, flower beds, playgrounds and sports grounds
questions.explain: Both stopping and parking are prohibited on flower beds, lawns, playgrounds and sports grounds. The other places listed are allowed if there are no other prohibitions.

questions.q: Which vehicles may be parked on the carriageway in two rows?
options: Passenger cars, if the hazard warning lights are on
Trucks, while they are unloading
Two-wheeled vehicles without a sidecar
None
questions.explain: On the carriageway, vehicles are parked in a single row parallel to the edge. The exception is two-wheeled vehicles without a sidecar: they may be parked in two rows.

questions.q: Where does this sign apply if it is placed at the right-hand edge of the street?
options: Only on the side where it is placed
On both sides of the street up to the nearest intersection
On both sides, if the street is narrow
Only for 25 m from where the sign is placed
questions.explain: Signs 3.27-3.30 apply only on the side of the road where they are placed. There is no ban on the opposite side unless it has its own sign or markings.

questions.q: Sign 3.28 is placed on a village street, and there are no intersections on this street before the end of the village. How far does the ban apply?
options: Up to the nearest exit from a yard
For 100 m from the sign
Up to the end of the built-up area
Up to the nearest bus stop
questions.explain: Signs 3.27-3.30 apply up to the nearest intersection beyond them or, in a built-up area with no intersection, up to the end of the built-up area. Exits from yards do not interrupt the sign's effect.

questions.q: These signs are placed on opposite sides of the same street. What does the time from 19:00 to 21:00 mean?
options: The time when parking is prohibited on both sides of the street at once
The time when only taxis are exempt from the signs
The time when only trucks are allowed to park
The time for moving cars from one side of the street to the other
questions.explain: Sign 3.29 prohibits parking on odd days, and 3.30 on even days. When they are placed on opposite sides of a street, vehicles are moved from one side to the other from 19:00 to 21:00.

questions.q: Who may stop in a route vehicle stop area and within 15 m of it?
options: Any vehicle, for boarding and alighting
Taxis with the taximeter on
Buses of categories M2 and M3
Passenger cars, for up to 1 minute
questions.explain: Stopping in stop areas and within 15 m of them is prohibited for everyone except vehicles of categories M2 and M3, that is, buses. There is no exception for taxis or passenger cars.

questions.q: Stopping is prohibited if there is less than 3 m between the vehicle and a solid marking line and this obstructs traffic. Which solid line does this rule not take into account?
options: A double solid line
A line separating opposing traffic flows
A line marking the edge of the carriageway
A line separating lanes in the same direction
questions.explain: The 3 m rule takes into account solid marking lines, except the line marking the edge of the carriageway. At the edge, a car always stands next to such a line, and this does not obstruct other drivers.

questions.q: Where is parking prohibited but a short stop allowed?
options: On a pedestrian crossing
In a tunnel
Within 50 m of a level crossing
Within 30 m of the edge of the intersecting carriageway
questions.explain: Within 50 m of a level crossing only parking is prohibited; you may stop there, for example, to drop off a passenger. On a pedestrian crossing, in a tunnel and within 30 m of an intersection, even stopping is prohibited.

questions.q: Who is exempt from this sign?
options: Route vehicles
Taxis with the taximeter on
Vehicles driven by persons with group I or II disabilities
Vehicles with the hazard warning lights on
questions.explain: Sign 3.27 “No stopping” does not apply to route vehicles. Taxis with the taximeter on and vehicles of persons with disabilities are exempt only from signs 3.28-3.30, which prohibit parking; in the zone of sign 3.27, a driver with a disability may stop only with the vehicle entirely on the pavement ⟦16⟧.

questions.q: At what visibility of the road is stopping on the carriageway near a dangerous bend prohibited?
options: Less than 100 m in at least one direction
Less than 300 m in both directions
Less than 50 m in both directions
Less than 150 m in at least one direction
questions.explain: Stopping on the carriageway near dangerous bends and brows of hills (convex changes in the longitudinal profile of the road) is prohibited if visibility of the road is less than 100 m in at least one direction.

questions.q: A truck with a maximum authorised mass of 10 t and a blue passenger car have been standing here for more than an hour. Who is allowed to park like this?
options: Only the truck
Only the blue car
Both the truck and the blue car
Neither the truck nor the blue car
questions.explain: A plate showing a truck makes sign 3.28 apply only to trucks with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3.5 t. The blue passenger car may park here.

questions.q: The plate under the sign shows 20 m. The blue car is 10 m beyond the sign, the red car 50 m. Who may stop here?
options: Both the blue and the red car
Neither the blue nor the red car
Only the blue car
Only the red car
questions.explain: The “Zone of application” plate with an arrow and a distance shows that sign 3.27 applies only for 20 m from where it is placed. The blue car is within this zone, and the red car is further on, where there is no longer a ban.

questions.q: Tram tracks run down the middle of a street in town, and there is one lane for vehicles in each direction. May you stop at the left-hand edge?
options: Yes: this is a built-up area with one lane in each direction
Yes, if no tram can be seen nearby
No: there are tram tracks in the middle
questions.explain: In built-up areas you may stop on the left on roads with one lane for each direction, but only if there are no tram tracks in the middle. Here there are tracks, and to stop on the left you would have to cross them.
